newsitem.title: USA: Maine asked to issue bonds for Portland terminal.
newsitem.headline: Maine asked to issue bonds for Portland terminal.

text.p: Portland officials have asked the state to issue $10 million in bonds to finance an expansion of its increasingly busy marine cargo facility.
The money would be used to buy land and a new crane and expanded warf at the facility, which has seen container loadings increase by 30 percent last year, officials said.
The bond request must be approved by the Legislature.
The city-owned facility is used by German shipping company Hapag-Lloyd AG as a feeder port to the company's larger marine loading facilities in Halifax and New York.
Portland is the second Maine marine facility considering an expansion.
The state has also been aproached by Bangor and Aroostook Railroad for help in upgrading its rail-to-ship transfer facility in Searsport.
